item.title: Neville warns managers can need sacking ‘for their own good’ as Carrick fights on
item.description: Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to dismissed “for their own good” as Manchester United persist with under-pressure boss Michael Carrick. Carrick’s future at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 humbling at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone. United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years. But former United and England midfielder Carrick, 45, remains in charge and is expected to give a pre-match press conference later Thursday ahead of the team’s league match away to Chelsea on Saturday. “I reckon what’s happened in the 24 hours after Bournemouth is that they (the United hierarchy) literally debated it (Carrick’s future) back and forth,” former Manchester United captain Neville said on the Stick to Football podcast. “I don’t know this, but they’ve debated it to the point where they’ve got themselves into a muddle, and thought, ‘we’ll just stay with him’. “I think staying with him is a result of the lack of planning, the lack of probably available options, the lack of decision-making around the two people that probably are available. That’s when you’re really struggling.” Neville, a former United team-mate of Carrick, added: “Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good. I needed sacking at Valencia. I was happy that they put me out of my misery.” – ‘Enough is enough’ – Both Eddie Howe, previously in charge of Newcastle, and former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann have been touted as possible replacements for Carrick at Old Trafford. Carrick, however, appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. The drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. Neville believes the root of United’s woes is majority owners the Glazer family, saying “enough is enough” as he urged them to sell-up. The Glazers took control of the club in a controversial takeover in 2005. They remain majority owners after selling a minority stake to British billionaire businessman Jim Ratcliffe in 2024 . Neville, a longstanding critic, reiterated his call for the US-based family to sell. “There’s £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion) of debt in that football club, they’re hamstrung in some ways,” said Neville

item.title: Tinubu has broken Imo’s shackles — Okorocha hails court judgment
item.description: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has praised President Bola Tinubu following a Federal High Court judgment recognising him as the All Progressives Congress candidate for Imo West Senatorial District, saying the ruling has broken the shackles holding the state. Okorocha spoke on Thursday while hosting his legal team after the judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court in Abuja. The court ruled that Okorocha won the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026, and ordered the party to submit his name to the Independent National Electoral Commission as its candidate for the January 16, 2027 senatorial election. The court also directed Governor Hope Uzodimma to stop parading himself as the party’s candidate. Reacting to the judgment, Okorocha thanked the judiciary for standing on the side of justice, describing the outcome as a victory for the people of Imo State. “I thank the judiciary for standing on the side of justice. I could imagine what would have happened in the state if they decided to twist justice. This is a victory for Imo State,” he said. The former governor also linked the judgment to the symbolic shackle on Tinubu’s traditional cap, suggesting that the President’s position had become clearer through the court’s decision. “This is also the first time the Imo people will understand the sign of the shackle on President Tinubu’s cap. By this judgment, the shackle on Imo State has been broken, and it is also evident that the President is tired of this nonsense and that he is not in support of it,” Okorocha said. He expressed gratitude to Tinubu, although he did not provide direct evidence that the President had intervened in the legal dispute or influenced the court’s decision. The judgment followed a legal battle in which Okorocha challenged INEC’s recognition of Uzodimma as the APC’s candidate for Imo West. The dispute attracted further attention earlier this month after INEC petitioned the police and the Department of State Services over a disputed document circulating online that purported to name Okorocha as the winner of the primary. INEC maintained that its official report recognised Uzodimma as the winner. Okorocha also addressed reports surrounding his alleged arrest, saying he deliberately refrained from commenting when the news broke. “When the news broke out that I was arrested, I refused to make any comments,” he said. He, however, questioned the documents presented during the dispute over the APC primary, particularly the claims that Uzodimma emerged through consensus and the discrepancies he alleged in the dates recorded in the documents. Okorocha questioned how a document could indicate that Uzodimma emerged through consensus when, according to him, individual scores were recorded. item.title: ‘Horrific’ Russian Drone Strike Kills 14 At Ukraine Train Station
item.description: A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine’s Dnipro on Thursday killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a “horrific” attack that demands a response from Kyiv’s allies. The strike came as Ukraine and Russia strive to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky — under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. The truce was holding into its third day, both countries said, with the Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets announcing that he had “set out with the Ukrainian delegation towards Oleshky” through Belarus and Russia. But elsewhere, Moscow continued to pummel Ukraine. The strike at the Dnipro train station hit a platform “where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing”, Zelensky said. By early Thursday afternoon, Dnipropetrovsk regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha said the death toll from the strike had risen to 14. EDITORS NOTE: Graphic content / In this handout photograph taken and released by the Ukrainian Emergency Service on October 29, 2026, Ukrainian law enforcement officers work at the site of an air attack on the railway station in Dnipro, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Photo by Handout / UKRAINIAN EMERGENCY SERVICE / AFP) Another 14 had been wounded, he said, adding that six of them were in severe condition after suffering “multiple shrapnel wounds”, including an 11-year-old boy and a man who had “both legs amputated”. Zelensky slammed the attack as “horrific” and insisted that “sanctions against Moscow and its war machine must not be eased for as long as this Russian war continues”. Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies on the platform, rescuers helping victims to safety and two burnt-out passenger trains with their windows shattered. French President Emmanuel Macron reacted with outrage to the attack, stressing the need for “far more than a localised ceasefire” like the one in Oleshky. “It is intolerable that Russia continues to reject all proposals to this end, choosing instead to pursue escalation and target civilians,” he said on X. Zelensky slams sanctions relief Russia has fired drones on trains across Ukraine since the first days of its 2022 invasion — destroying hundreds of locomotives and killing several railway workers. Ukraine’s air force said it had intercepted three jet-powered drones in a daytime attack, but that a fourth evaded its defences and hit the station. In the aftermath of the attack, Zelensky refreshed his criticism of a deal struck this month between US President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to ease some sanctions on Russia allowing Moscow to release diesel onto global markets. “How many such terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on some Russian oligarchs and the energy sector, instead of de-escalating,” he asked. item.title: Meet Nigerian Engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi behind machine that braids hair five times faster
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian-born engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi is gaining attention for developing HaloBraid, an automated hair braiding device designed to help professional stylists complete hairstyles up to five times faster while reducing the physical strain associated with hours of braiding. Ogunbiyi, a Harvard graduate and biomechanical engineer, recently demonstrated how the technology works, offering a glimpse into how automation could transform the hair and beauty industry, particularly protective hairstyles that often require several hours to complete. Unlike a machine that replaces the stylist entirely, HaloBraid is designed to work alongside professional hairdressers. The stylist first sections the hair, applies the necessary products and starts the braid by hand before feeding it into the device. The machine then handles the repetitive weaving along the length of the hair, allowing the stylist to finish and seal the ends. The innovation aims to reduce the time spent on braiding while easing the physical demands placed on stylists who spend long hours working with clients. It also seeks to improve the salon experience without removing the human skill involved in creating the final hairstyle. Ogunbiyi said the inspiration for the invention came from her personal experience of getting her hair braided from childhood and the challenges she repeatedly observed among both stylists and clients. “My braid story starts at age four, sitting between my mum’s legs as she braided my hair for the first time. Since then, I’ve spent thousands of hours getting my hair braided — and heard the same story from stylists and clients again and again: braiding is beautiful, but it takes too much time and too much strain,” she said. Drawing on her background in biomechanical engineering, Ogunbiyi said she recognised the need for a better approach and developed HaloBraid in collaboration with hairstylists, designers and other professionals. She added that the device was built with people close to her in mind, including her mother, hairstylists and aunties, as well as others around the world who understand the experience of spending hours in a salon chair. The venture has also attracted significant investor interest, securing $7 million in seed funding in a round led by Seven Seven Six, the venture capital firm founded by Reddit co founder Alexis Ohanian, who is married to tennis champion Serena Williams. The development adds to Ogunbiyi’s growing recognition in innovation and entrepreneurship. Her HaloBraid project previously won a $75,000 Harvard Innovation Prize, highlighting the potential of the technology to address a familiar challenge in the beauty industry. With its latest demonstration, HaloBraid is positioning itself as a technology that combines traditional hairstyling expertise with automation, potentially giving stylists more time to serve clients while reducing the repetitive work involved in braiding. item.title: Indonesians Celebrate Rain After Months Of Smoke And Suffering
item.description: Residents and firefighters in an Indonesian city long shrouded in a toxic haze brought on by months of wildfires rushed outside dancing and chanting as rain this week brought a welcome respite. On Wednesday night, exhausted volunteer firefighters jumped around in the puddles and kissed the ground in gratitude as another burst came down. “We were overjoyed; every one of us volunteers was so happy that we prostrated ourselves in gratitude. Praise be to God that there was finally rain,” firefighter Lukman El Hakim told AFP. TOPSHOT – Indonesian soldiers, tasked with fighting forest and land fires, celebrate as it rains in Banjar Baru, South Kalimantan province on October 28, 2026, following months of forest and land fires. (Photo by MUDA SAGALA / AFP) | MUDA SAGALA / AFP Intermittent rains have been falling in Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan province on Indonesian Borneo, where devastating wildfires have raged since August. The city’s air quality index hit 4,000 this month, its worst ever measurement and more than 13 times the environment ministry’s threshold for pollution deemed “hazardous” to health. More than 11,000 people have been treated for respiratory infections in Palangkaraya during the months-long crisis that has also affected Indonesia’s neighbours with haze pollution. The World Health Organisation has linked exposure to air pollution, including high levels of tiny, airborne PM2.5 particles, to increased risk of illness and premature death. A volunteer (R) assists a woman with a nasal oxygen cannula at a shelter run by the Central Kalimantan Forest and Land Fire Smoke Response Coalition (RAKAT) to aid residents experiencing respiratory difficulties in Palangkaraya, Central Kalimantan.More than 11,000 people have been treated for respiratory infections in Palangkaraya during a months-long wildfire crisis. At least 11 people have died fighting Indonesia’s wildfires, most recently a 45-year-old forest ranger who was killed by a falling tree while battling flames in North Toraja, South Sulawesi, on Wednesday. Palangkaraya resident Muhammad Jihan Alwi used the reprieve to jog outdoors for the first time in months. “Of course I’m happy to be out jogging again, breathing in fresh air that’s better than yesterday, just feeling grateful,” the 23-year-old said, smiling. item.title: 2027: Abia CP warns politicians against violence, intimidation
item.description: …Orders parties to notify police before rallies . We ‘re for nobody, we ‘re for everybody – REC, urges candidates to accept results or seek redress in court By Steve Oko UMUAHIA – The Abia State Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, has warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and destruction of property ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is as the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its neutrality in the 2027 Abia governorship election, assuring all candidates that it will provide a level playing field for every contestant. CP Afolabi, who spoke at the signing of a peace accord involving the NEC, security agencies and political parties in Umuahia, urged parties to notify the police in writing before holding rallies, processions and other political activities to enable adequate security arrangements. The meeting, held at the Police Officers’ Mess, Umuahia, was attended by INEC’s Resident Electoral Commissioner in Abia, Prof. Sylvia Agu, heads of sister security agencies and representatives of registered political parties and campaign teams. The Police boss reaffirmed the command’s commitment to providing professional, impartial and adequate security for all candidates, parties and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation. He disclosed that the command had strengthened its security architecture through intelligence gathering and analysis, crime mapping, the revamp of its Cybercrime Unit and improved operational response mechanisms. Afolabi also acknowledged Governor Alex Otti’s directive on adequate security for political campaigns and related activities. He pledged continued collaboration with INEC, other security agencies and political stakeholders to protect lives and property and ensure a peaceful electoral process. The peace accord, which followed a review of relevant electoral laws by the command’s legal officer, was subsequently read to the stakeholders before representatives of political parties signed individually, pledging to pursue their political ambitions peacefully. Speaking at the event, the REC, Prof. Agu, said the commission was committed to serving all candidates equally, irrespective of their political parties, while urging them to maintain peace before, during and after the election. “We are not working for any particular party; we are working for all of you here. We are going to deliver on our mandate, but we are asking you to conduct yourselves properly,” she said. The REC urged candidates to accept the outcome of a free, fair and credible election, advising those dissatisfied with the results to seek redress through the judiciary rather than resort to violence or discredit the electoral process. She stressed that electoral contests inevitably produce winners and losers, urging candidates to demonstrate sportsmanship regardless of the outcome. “In any contest, there must be a winner and a loser. item.description: TUC rejects ₦70,000 transport allowance as proposed scheme could cost ₦465.7 billion The Trade Union Congress has rejected the Federal Government’s temporary ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for federal workers, demanding a permanent salary increase instead. President Bola Tinubu during the inauguration of the APC PCC. The government agreed with the Nigeria Labour Congress on Tuesday to provide the allowance for six months, beginning in November. However, a Punch analysis estimates that the programme could cost ₦465.7 billion over six months if all 1.1 million employee records on the federal payroll qualify. This is an estimate, not an officially approved expenditure figure. TUC President Festus Osifo argues that earlier temporary wage awards were inconsistently implemented and failed to reach many eligible workers. Why it matters: What appeared to be a breakthrough in labour negotiations has exposed disagreement within organised labour. The government must now address both the affordability of its proposed intervention and workers’ demands for permanent improvements in income. Watch: The government’s response to the TUC, final eligibility rules, the funding source and whether the NLC–government agreement proceeds as scheduled. INEC meets today to decide fate of Pantami, Adebutu and other excluded candidates INEC The Independent National Electoral Commission is considering petitions from parties whose governorship candidates were excluded from its published list for the February 6, 2027 elections. INEC National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna confirmed that the commission would examine the matter at today’s meeting. Affected candidates include Isa Pantami of the PDP in Gombe, Ladi Adebutu of the PDP in Ogun and Aminu Gwarzo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Kano. Several exclusions followed disputes over party nominations and compliance with membership-register requirements under the Electoral Act. No final decision from today’s meeting had been verified at this editorial cut-off. Why it matters: The commission’s decisions could determine which candidates appear on governorship ballots and whether additional court challenges become necessary. Watch: INEC’s formal decisions, publication of corrected candidate lists and legal responses from affected parties. item.title: Alleged assault: Ivan Toney to stand trial in June 2028
item.description: England striker Ivan Toney will face trial over an alleged assault at a nightclub in June 2028, it was announced Thursday. The 30-year-old, who plays for Saudi club Al-Ahli, is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva at a club in the Soho area of central London last December. Toney appeared at London’s Southwark Crown Court on Thursday and formally entered a not guilty plea to a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm. During the five-minute hearing, a provisional trial date was set for the same court on June 12, 2028 by Judge Christopher Hehir, who told Toney he was “sorry” about the delay. “That’s a long way in advance and I’m sorry about that,” said Hehir. “As you may know, the crown courts are operating under a great deal of pressure. We have got a massive backlog of work for various reasons.” Toney was released on unconditional bail after the brief hearing. An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Da Silva. It was heard the two men “squared up to each other”, before Toney allegedly “lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches”. The former Brentford player has played for England 10 times, scoring one goal. He was a member of the 2026 World Cup squad but is not in the latest Nations League squad. item.title: Facebook partners Funke Akindele to promote Nigerian storytelling
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Social media platform Facebook has partnered with Nollywood filmmaker and actor Funke Akindele to promote Nigerian storytelling at the London and Lagos premieres of her new film, The Four . The partnership will support the film’s world premiere in London and its homecoming premiere in Lagos, bringing creators, celebrities and audiences together. Meta’s Head of Communications for Sub-Saharan Africa, Oluwasola Obagbemi, said the collaboration would highlight how Facebook helps creators connect with fans and build communities around shared interests. “Facebook has always been about connecting people, and our partnership with Funke Akindele brings that to life through film,” Obagbemi said. He said creators on Facebook could reach global audiences, build relationships with fans and earn money from original content. “Through our partnership around The Four premieres in London and Lagos, we’re celebrating the creators shaping culture, and helping more creators who share original and engaging content on Facebook to succeed,” he said. Akindele said she was pleased to partner with Facebook to take Nigerian stories to wider audiences. “African cinema has always had beautiful stories for the world to enjoy, and it’s exciting to have Facebook as a partner in bringing these stories to even more audiences globally,” she said. The partnership will also spotlight Nigerian creators in the country and in the diaspora. A creator-hosted space at the premieres will capture social content on how creators use Facebook to reach younger audiences and share Nigerian stories and culture beyond the country’s borders. Akindele announced the partnership on her Facebook page. The company said audiences could follow the Meta Africa, officialfunkeAkindele, Funke Akindele and Fanntv Facebook pages for behind-the-scenes content from the premieres. The collaboration, it said, celebrates Nollywood’s global reach and the creators and communities helping Nigerian stories travel. item.title: EPL: Man City braced for another tough test in Brighton repeat
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has warned his side to expect no let-up from Brighton this weekend when the teams meet again just days after a dramatic cup tie. League Cup-holders City edged the Seagulls on penalties to reach the quarter-finals on Wednesday after twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 at the Etihad Stadium. After making 16 changes between them, both Maresca and Brighton counterpart Fabian Hurzeler are set to revert to their full-strength sides when the teams meet in the Premier League at the Etihad on Saturday. Table-toppers City are level on points with champions Arsenal, while third-placed Brighton are just five points behind the leading duo. “They (Brighton) are in a brilliant moment,” said Maresca. “They are winning games, they are scoring goals. They are scoring many goals every game –- three, four, five, goals a game. “I’ve watched all their Premier League games since we started, and since the first day –- against Arsenal, (Crystal) Palace, Liverpool, they always go front foot, man to man. “We knew that this was a tough game and they’re going to be exactly the same on Saturday,” added Maresca. Brighton went in front after 30 minutes when Malick Yalcouye steered Georginio Rutter’s shot past Geronimo Rulli from five yards. Mateo Kovacic hauled City level 20 minutes later with a fine finish that curled into the far corner from 25 yards. Rutter restored Brighton’s lead two minutes after half-time, slotting home from Jaouen Hadjam’s cut-back. Vitor Reis deflected in Rayan Cherki’s 72nd-minute free-kick to equalise for City. Kovacic’s penalty was saved by Jason Steele in the shoot-out, but Rulli denied Brighton’s Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight. City’s season continues under the shadow of being found guilty last month on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict. No punishment has yet been announced, however, and Maresca — who has repeatedly stated his complete trust in City’s hierarchy — remains focused on on-field issues, with his side drawn at home to third-tier Bradford in the League Cup quarter-finals. “It’s a different competition but the ambition has to be the same,” said Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola after the Spaniard stepped down at the end of last season following a trophy-laden decade at the Etihad. “This is a new project with new players, a new manager. It started three months ago. “We need to do our business. item.title: Court sacks Uzodinma as APC senatorial candidate for Imo West
item.description: …orders INEC to recognise ex-Gov Okorocha By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday nullified the emergence of Governor Hope Uzodinma as candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the Imo West Senatorial election slated for January 16, 2027. The court, in a judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, held that evidence before it established that Governor Uzodinma was not the valid winner of the primary election the APC conducted in the senatorial zone on May 18, which was monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). According to the court, it was a former governor of the state, Senator Rochas Okorocha, who garnered the highest number of votes cast at the primary election and therefore ought to have been nominated by the party. Consequently, Justice Egwuatu ordered INEC to forthwith recognise Senator Okorocha and publish his name as the authentic candidate of the APC for the senatorial poll. It further issued an order barring Governor Uzodinma from presenting himself as the candidate of the APC for the election. item.title: Iran Guards says three tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that three oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz. “Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz,” the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement. The vessels had “switched off all their radar and navigation systems” and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said. It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying. Since the outbreak of the war on February 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil and gas consumption. The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports. Iran’s armed forces have repeatedly accused US Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees US military operations in the region, of encouraging vessels to use a southern corridor near the Omani coast that Tehran considers unauthorised. “The IRGC Navy states that the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to CENTCOM’s delusions on social media,” the statement said. Earlier on Thursday, the British maritime agency UKMTO said it had received a report of a ship on fire in the strait but gave no details about the cause or any casualties. It was not immediately clear if it was one of the three ships referred to by the Guards. The organisation also said it had captured a US reconnaissance drone during an operation in the Strait of Hormuz in a separate statement. “The IRGC Navy announced that its electronic warfare unit had successfully captured a US MQM-170 drone during an offensive operation in the western Strait of Hormuz,” the statement said. item.title: Stop the Bloodshed: Pyrates demands action from Tinubu, Kefas in Taraba
item.description: The National Association of Seadogs (Pyrates Confraternity) demanded decisive action from President Bola Tinubu and the Taraba State governor, Agbu Kefas, over the killing of at least 58 people in Binari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area. The group also tasked security agencies to discontinue all peace arrangements that have enabled terror groups to rearm. The NAS Cap’n, Dr Charles Meribole, in a statement entitled ‘’ The Taraba Massacre: Another Bloodbath in Our Nation, ” condemned what he called ‘’senseless killings’’ of Nigerians, noting that it was ‘’barbaric, reprehensible and must not go unpunished “ Meribole, while mourning the dead, expressed disappointment with the response of Nigeria’s political leadership and the security agencies to recurring killings, especially in Northern Nigeria. He lamented that the over 20,000 Nigerians who have been killed since May 29, 2023, when President Tinubu assumed office, should jolt the President to rise to the full weight of his office as President and Commander-in- Chief of the Armed Forces and end Nigeria’s security crisis. ‘’President Bola Tinubu should recognise that the security of Nigerians is not a peripheral issue to be addressed when convenient or tackled with political rhetoric. It is a central test of his administration’s responsibility to Nigerians and obligation to his oath of office. ‘’ We implore President Bola Tinubu to translate his directives to the security agencies into measurable results. His orders to dismantle criminal networks must come with clear timelines, effective monitoring and consequences for failure. Those implementing security operations must be held accountable for their performance, and any official found to have compromised these efforts must face the appropriate consequences.’’ Meribole upbraided Kefas for attending the All Progressives Congress 2027 Presidential campaign (APC) North-West campaign flag-off, noting that traumatised people of Binari deserve empathy and not empty promises. He called on the security agencies to discharge their duties with renewed determination, stressing that since terror groups have demonstrated that they are remorseless, they should be treated with equal measure through sustained and decisive security operations. The statement read in part ‘’ President Bola Tinubu’s recent marching orders to dismantle terrorists and bandits’ enclaves, rescue kidnapped citizens and restore public confidence in the government’s capacity to protect lives and property must be pursued with sustained commitment. ‘’ There must be no retreat, no complacency and no room for compromise with those who terrorise innocent Nigerians. item.title: NFF warned me against inviting Mikel, Enyeama, Emenike — Oliseh
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Super Eagles coach, Sunday Oliseh, has revealed that the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) warned him against inviting John Obi Mikel, Vincent Enyeama and Emmanuel Emenike to the national team when he took charge, describing the trio as players who were causing problems for the federation. Oliseh, speaking on The Play Zone Podcast, however, said he regretted not heeding the warning, recalling his efforts to engage the players individually and resolve issues surrounding their involvement with the national team. “I regret not having listened to the NFF. Because when I took over the job, the first thing NFF told me was to stop inviting three of them (Mikel, Enyeama and Emenike) because they were chaotic to the NFF,” he said. Oliseh recalled travelling from Belgium to France to meet Enyeama, who was playing for Lille at the time, saying he held discussions with the former Super Eagles captain and clarified matters with him. He said he also travelled to London at his own expense to meet Mikel and Victor Moses, who were both playing in England at the time, but was disappointed when Mikel failed to attend the scheduled meeting. “I did the same thing for Obi Mikel. With my own money, not the NFF money, I went to the UK, sent a message to the clubs, sent a message to him (Mikel), sent message not only to him but also to Victor Moses, gave them an appointment at a bar that was accessible in the heart of London, with my assistant coach, for two of them to come and have meeting. “Now, of the two of them, who did not come to the meeting? Obi Mikel did not come to the meeting. Victor Moses came. Obi Mikel did not even respond to the WhatsApp message,” he said. The former midfielder suggested that Mikel might have considered himself bigger than the national team coach because he was playing for a major club. “Maybe because he’ll say, ‘I play for this big club now,’ but you see, that’s why they say sometimes Sunday (Oliseh) is direct. Where did you play that I did not play? What did you play that I did not play? “Even though the coach was not a footballer or not as big as you, the fact that they’ve given him that title ‘national team coach’, means you have to respect the position he’s holding,” Oliseh added. He described Mikel’s failure to attend the meeting as one of the biggest insults he had experienced but said he did not take the incident personally. According to Oliseh, Moses used the meeting to explain the issues troubling him about the national team, including some experiences Oliseh said he could relate to. Oliseh also spoke positively about Emenike, saying his experience working with the former striker contradicted what he had initially been told about him. He described Emenike as a gentleman and a respectful player, adding that he was among the greatest footballers he worked with and also credited Emenike’s influence as an important factor in Nigeria’s triumph at the 2013 Africa Cup of Nations. item.title: Tell Nigerians your real destination, APM challenges Tinubu
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Allied People’s Movement, APM, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to disclose his actual destination, insisting that he should remain in Nigeria to pray for the country and tackle the hardship facing citizens. The party argued that Tinubu should address Nigeria’s mounting problems at home rather than embark on a trip, it questioned, alleging that the announced lesser Hajj pilgrimage should not serve as a cover for other activities. In a statement, APM National Publicity Secretary Abubakar Yusuf questioned the purpose of the President’s trip, insisting that the pilgrimage should not be used to distract from the challenges confronting Nigerians. “Lesser Hajj involves prayer and supplications, but not an opportunity to do the unusual or as a cover to do other things,” Yusuf said. Accusing Tinubu’s administration of worsening the hardship in the country, the APM spokesman said the president should stay back and address the problems facing ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot pray for the problems you have inflicted on ordinary Nigerians, rather than staying here to resolve the heavily burdened, self-contrived problems of the citizens,” he said. Yusuf also invoked the popular ‘Andrew, check out’ expression, urging Tinubu not to leave the country. “Let Mr President not behave like ‘Andrew’ of those days, saying President Bola Ahmed Tinubu should not check out,” he said. Looking ahead to the 2027 presidential election, Yusuf claimed Tinubu could struggle to secure the required 25 per cent of votes in 12 selected states, challenging the president to pay attention to his electoral prospects. The APM spokesman expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, would defeat Tinubu in 2027, describing him as a workaholic and energetic contender poised to challenge the President’s political dominance in the South-West and across the South. item.title: ‘This abuse must end’ – Sowore reacts to remand of Doris Ogala
item.description: Human rights activist, Omoyele Sowore, has condemned the remand of actress Doris Ogala at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre pending the hearing and determination of her bail application over alleged cyberbullying, cyberstalking and attempted extortion of Pastor Chris Okafor. Ogala was arraigned Wednesday on three counts by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation before Justice Akintayo Aluko of the Federal High Court in Lagos on allegations bordering on the publication of intimate photographs, dissemination of allegedly false electronic messages and threats against the cleric. The prosecution counsel, Tolulope Mokolu, told the court that between September 2024 and March 2026, Ogala published nude and intimate photographs of Okafor on her social media accounts without his consent. He alleged that the publication was capable of causing annoyance, embarrassment, emotional distress and injury to the cleric’s reputation. In his reaction on Facebook, Sowore accused the police of weaponising the Cybercrimes Act to serve the interest of “influential figures”. “Once again, the Nigeria Police Force has deepened its weaponization of the Cybercrimes Act! What kind of society are we becoming? How could anyone be arraigned simply over allegations of having an affair with a pastor? And how could the police actually take such a matter before a Federal High Court judge? “Even more troubling is that the case has reportedly been brought before Justice Aluko of the Federal High Court in Lagos, a judge whose handling of cases involving pastors raises serious concerns about judicial impartiality. The perception that the police and judiciary are being used to settle personal scores and protect influential religious figures must be confronted. “The Nigeria Police Force has no business turning private relationships into criminal prosecutions or deploying the Cybercrimes Act as a weapon of intimidation,” he wrote. Sowore noted that Ogala, as the governorship candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC) in Abia State, deserves the full protection of her constitutional rights, due process, and a fair hearing. “The police must stop criminalizing private disputes, and the judiciary must never become an instrument of religious influence or personal vendettas. This abuse must end!” he added. Ogala’s case was adjourned until October 30, 2026, for the hearing of her bail application. item.title: Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga face long road to redemption in China
item.description: Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the superstar striker’s comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China won’t be easily or quickly repaired, experts say. The France captain, one of the best footballers on the planet, is at the centre of a major row after a video emerged this week of him appearing to make fun of former leader Mao. Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”. Mao remains officially revered as the hero of the communist revolution and founder of the People’s Republic of China. He is blamed by historians for millions of deaths, but publicly mocking him is taboo, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure or entity to infuriate Beijing. Major Chinese brands cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish top-flight matches will be pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV. Chinese state media and social media users lined up to lambast Mbappe, although they were left in the dark about what exactly he said. China has the world’s second-biggest economy and can be hugely lucrative, and within two days the striker, his club Real Madrid, and La Liga all apologised. A spokesman for China’s foreign ministry said the Beijing government took Mbappe’s apology “seriously”. – ‘Serious damage’ – So is that the end of the matter? “Viewed from a calm, objective and emotion-free standpoint, this is clearly a very damaging incident,” Yan Qiang, a veteran sports commentator, told AFP. “It causes serious damage to the image of La Liga and Real Madrid in China. “In the age of the mobile internet things blow up on social media quickly and emotions run high. “An apology does not necessarily mean the end of the story. “It’s better to have an apology than no apology at all, but it’s definitely not the end of the story.” The Mbappe furore and fallout is not an unfamiliar tale. Various overseas sports leagues or players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China. China effectively cut ties with the NBA in 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters. NBA executives said Morey had the right to freedom of expression. In contrast, La Liga immediately distanced itself from what Mbappe said. The NBA, which along with football is the most popular sport in China, was wiped from CCTV for more than a year. NBA pre-season matches only returned to China last year. Australian National University lecturer Debby Chan called the NBA case — and now Mbappe — an illustration of China’s consumer nationalism, where online sentiment and state media converge into “a spiral of outrage”. NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the league lost “hundreds of millions of dollars” over the split. – No way back? – Spanish football also has a lot to lose. item.title: ‘Nigeria dodged a massive howitzer,’ Keyamo slams Obi over public funds comment
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has criticised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, over his claim that Nigeria could be wealthier if public funds were kept in banks to earn interest. Reacting in a post on his X account on Wednesday, Keyamo described Obi’s remarks as unintelligent and linked them to what he claimed was a decline in the former governor’s approval ratings. “This dumbness is beyond measure. I really don’t know whether to laugh or to cry. No wonder his approval ratings have plummeted so badly. “Nigeria did not just dodge a bullet; it ducked a massive howitzer!” Keyamo wrote. Vanguard had reported that Obi, speaking during an interview with a radio station in Nasarawa State on Wednesday, argued that Nigeria would be significantly wealthier if leaders left public funds in banks to generate interest instead of mismanaging the country’s resources. “I wish everybody in this country left money in the bank; they have interest. Nigeria would have been so rich that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said Obi also addressed questions surrounding his administration’s public engagements, explaining that he believed the results of government projects should speak for themselves because they were financed with public funds. “We did what we were doing with public money, so the public already see us working, so why are we going to do the ceremony or showing it on TV? Maybe I was wrong, but that was what happened,” he said. The post ‘Nigeria dodged a massive howitzer,’ Keyamo slams Obi over public funds comment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gombe @30: Yahaya seeks continuity ahead of 2027
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya of Gombe State has called for continuity in governance, political unity and sustained investment in critical sectors as the state marks 30 years of creation, saying its future must transcend the ambitions of any individual or political party. Yahaya, reflecting on the state’s three-decade journey, said the anniversary provided an opportunity to celebrate past achievements and assess how statehood had translated into improved living conditions, expanded opportunities and inclusive development. The governor, whose second term ends in 2027, urged political leaders, traditional rulers, religious institutions, youths and other stakeholders to approach the forthcoming political transition with responsibility, peace and commitment to the collective interest of the state. Speaking against the backdrop of the anniversary theme, “Reflecting on our History, Consolidating Progress, and Charting the Future,” Yahaya said successive generations must understand the state’s history, preserve developmental gains and build institutions capable of outlasting individual administrations. He also highlighted achievements recorded under his administration in education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, industrialisation, electricity, environmental protection, public service reform and grassroots development. Gombe State was created on October 1, 1996, by the late General Sani Abacha following years of agitation for greater political representation, accelerated development and governance closer to the people. Yahaya expressed gratitude to Abacha and the state’s founding fathers and mothers, saying their contributions laid the foundation on which successive administrations had built. “Thirty years ago, a dream that our people had carried for generations finally became a reality. It was the recognition of a longstanding aspiration for greater representation, accelerated development, political inclusion and a stronger voice within the Nigerian federation,” he said. He, however, noted that state creation alone did not guarantee development, stressing that its value lay in expanding opportunities, deepening inclusion, improving governance and enhancing citizens’ welfare. According to him, Gombe’s development cannot be credited to any single administration, political party or individual, describing governance as a relay in which each generation must advance the work of its predecessors. The governor paid tribute to the state’s pioneer military administrators, Group Captain Joseph Orji and Lieutenant Colonel Mohammed Inuwa Bawa, for establishing the machinery of government and laying the institutional foundations of the state. item.title: Judicial Reform: NBA’s unheeded proposal to restructure NJC
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri About two and a half years ago, precisely in April 2024, the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) proposed a bold reform to remove the Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, as the statutory chairman of the National Judicial Council, NJC. The NBA, as the umbrella body of legal practitioners in the country, faulted the composition of the Council, which is saddled with the responsibility of disciplining erring judicial officers. It not only challenged the current system, which mandates that the Council be headed by the CJN, but also demanded a review of its composition. According to the NBA: “The inherent flaws in the composition of the NJC impact negatively on its ability to prosecute judicial misconduct in a manner that inspires public confidence.” As part of its recommendations, the Bar proposed that the NJC be constituted as follows: six judicial officers appointed by the CJN; six lawyers nominated by the National Executive Council of the NBA, including the NBA President; and six non-lawyers appointed by the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, subject to Senate approval. “The Chairmanship of these bodies should be rotated between the heads of the three constituent groups,” the NBA insisted. Furthermore, the association recommended appointing court administrators to assume the administrative functions currently performed by the heads of court, including procurement, budgeting, court renovation, and the implementation of judicial appropriations. “These are activities within court administration that have severally been identified by the anti-corruption bodies as areas prone to corrupt activities. “This proposal for the creation of this office takes cognizance of the role of the Chief Registrars of courts who will under the proposed arrangements enable them (together with heads of courts) to concentrate solely on the business of adjudication especially case management without distraction.” The recommendations were contained in proposals the NBA submitted at a national summit on Justice Sector reforms. The Chairman of the Joint Planning Committee of the summit, Dr. Babatunde Ajibade, SAN, had, at that time, told newsmen that the reform proposals were considered and approved in modified form. “The general consensus reached by this panel was that the role of the NJC in discharging its responsibility for judicial appointments into the Superior Courts of Record required significant review. “There was a concern expressed about the fact that the CJN, who is the chairman of the NJC is also the chairman of the Federal Judicial Service Commission, which is the body that initially reviews proposals or lists of candidates for appointment into judicial office. “The members pointed out the seeming inconsistency between the CJN playing both those roles, as it would appear that he was then recommending candidates to himself being chairman of both bodies, and being the person who appoints a significant number of the members of both bodies other t

item.title: Kalu opposes plenary invitation to INEC chairman
item.description: The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has opposed a proposal to invite the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, to brief the House on preparations for the 2027 general elections, arguing that the engagement could distract the commission. Kalu made the position known during Wednesday’s plenary while contributing to a motion jointly sponsored by the Minority Whip, Mansur Soro, and the Deputy Minority Leader, Abdulsamad Dasuki, seeking to invite the INEC chairman to address lawmakers on the commission’s preparations for the elections. Opposing the prayer seeking a plenary briefing, the deputy speaker argued that INEC’s recent public engagements were sufficient to address many of the concerns raised about the electoral process. He said further inquiries should be channelled through the House Committee on Electoral Matters, which has the mandate to interface with the commission on behalf of the legislature. According to Kalu, inviting the INEC chairman before the full House at this stage could create unnecessary pressure on the commission, trigger public anxiety and undermine confidence in the electoral process. He maintained that the commission had been engaging the public on its preparations and had not reported any logistical challenges. “I stand not in support of the prayer of this particular motion because supporting the prayer is belittling the mandate of the committee set up to carry out this function,” he said. Kalu questioned the need to summon Amupitan before the entire House shortly after his public briefing, urging lawmakers to have confidence in the relevant committees established to oversee the commission’s activities. “Inviting the chairman of INEC to come and brief the House when he just briefed the entire nation is not ideal. Don’t we believe in our committees again?” he asked. He proposed an amendment to the motion to require the INEC chairman to meet with the relevant committee rather than address the entire House at plenary. The deputy speaker also argued that the National Assembly, as an institution responsible for strengthening democracy, should support the electoral commission in carrying out its responsibilities rather than subjecting it to what he considered an ill-timed plenary inquiry. His proposed amendment was seconded by a member of the House, Babajimi Benson, who represents a constituency in Lagos State. When the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, put the motion to a voice vote, lawmakers overwhelmingly supported the amendment, after which he referred the matter to the House Committee on Electoral Matters. The committee is expected to handle the concerns raised in the motion and engage with INEC on its preparations for the 2027 general elections.
